title: Projections domain schema api/v0
description: Public API declarations: declaration entities carry `data.signature`, and optionally `data.contract`, their compatibility facts in terms every ecosystem shares.

constituent.description: One member of a union type.

text.description: The constituent as the language writes it, such as `"low"`.

primitive.description: The primitive it is, or a literal of it widens to, such as `string` or `undefined`; absent for other types.

typeRef.description: A type where values flow: its text as the language writes it, and, when the extractor resolves it, its union constituents.

text.description: The type as the language writes it, such as `System.Int32` or `number | undefined`.

union.description: Each constituent of the type, a single one when it is no union; absent when the extractor resolves no unions.

access.description: A property's accessors, each with who can use it; an accessor that is absent doesn't exist.

init.description: An accessor that sets it only while an instance is created: .NET `init`.

variadic.description: It takes any number of arguments: a TypeScript rest parameter, a .NET `params` array.

default.description: The value an omitted argument takes, as the language writes it.

passing.description: How the argument is passed: by `value`, or by reference as .NET `ref`, `out`, `in` and `ref readonly`.

attributes.description: The parameter's attributes, as the language writes them.

name.description: The parameter's name, such as `T` or Rust's lifetime `'a`.

constraints.description: What an argument must satisfy, each as the language writes it: bounds, constraints or a single constraint type.

default.description: The argument used when none is given.

type.description: A value parameter's type, such as a Rust `const` generic's `usize`.

signature.description: One way to call or construct a declaration.

returns.description: What a call returns; a constructor its instance, or the language's void.

returnAttributes.description: Attributes of what it returns, as the language writes them.

supertype.description: A type a declaration derives from or implements.

relation.description: Whether it derives from the type (a base class, a supertrait, an interface an interface extends) or implements it.

type.description: The type, as the language writes it.

contract.description: The language-neutral facts compatibility rules read about one declaration. Booleans that are absent are false. Facts only one ecosystem's rules read are in `native`.

declaration.description: What kind of declaration it is.

term.description: The ecosystem's own word for the kind of declaration, such as Rust's `trait-method`, Go's `func` or .NET's `record class`; a change of `term` is a change of kind.

static.description: It belongs to its type rather than to instances.

abstract.description: It has no implementation: implementers or subclasses must provide it (.NET `abstract` members and interface members without a default body, TypeScript's `abstract`, Rust trait items without a default, Go interface methods); a class that is abstract can't be instantiated.

sealed.description: Consumers can't inherit or implement it: a .NET type that is sealed, static or has no accessible constructor; a Rust trait with a supertrait outside the public API; a Go interface with unexported methods.

readonly.description: Consumers can read it but not assign it: .NET `readonly` fields, TypeScript `readonly` properties, Rust statics that aren't `mut`.

required.description: Code creating an instance must set it: .NET `required` members.

optional.description: It may be absent: a TypeScript optional (`?`) member.

nonExhaustive.description: It may gain members without a breaking change, so consumers may not match every variant or name every field in literals and patterns: Rust `#[non_exhaustive]`.

hiddenMembers.description: It has fields or variants consumers can't see, so they can't construct it from its fields or destructure it exhaustively: Rust private fields and hidden variants.

type.description: Its type: a field's, property's, variable's, constant's or event's; the type an alias names; the type an implementation is for; a Go function's or method's type.

value.description: A constant's or enum member's value, as the language writes it.

underlying.description: The type an enum or a defined type is represented by: a .NET enum's, a Go defined type's.

source.description: What a re-export re-exports, as a path.

attributes.description: Its attributes or annotations, each as the language writes it, such as .NET `System.ObsoleteAttribute("Use Run")`.

signatures.description: How it is called or constructed: one signature, or each overload in order. An indexer has one, whose parameters are its keys.

typeParameters.description: Its generic parameters; a callable's are its signatures'.

supertypes.description: What it derives from or implements, as its ecosystem lists them: .NET base types and every implemented interface, TypeScript heritage clauses, Rust supertraits and the trait an implementation implements, the Go interfaces of the package a type implements.

constraints.description: What an associated type must satisfy, each as the language writes it.

native.description: Ecosystem-specific facts, read only by that ecosystem's compatibility rules. Each public API extractor documents its own.

refinement.description: What `api/v0` adds to the extraction envelope.

signature.description: The declaration as source shows it, such as `(a: string) => void`.

contract.description: The facts compatibility rules read about the declaration, in terms every ecosystem shares.
